title: A bounded flat complex with finite cohomology over a Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $C$ be an object of the derived category $D(A\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that $C$ has a bounded representative by flat $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that every $H^i(C)$ is a finite (finitely generated) $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $C$ is represented by a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules, hence is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: Choose the bounded flat representative F and express its bounds as IsStrictlyGE and IsStrictlyLE. Transport finite cohomology from C to F using the homology comparison isomorphism. Choose the universe-u derived category of modules (HasDerivedCategory.ofIsGrothendieckAbelian), and transport finite cohomology to its image of F. Apply the already proved source-library theorem DerivedCategory.isPerfect_of_flat_of_finite_homology (WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Perfect.OfFlat), which realizes this same mathematical statement at universe u. Unpack IsPerfect to obtain a bounded finite projective complex P and an isomorphism between the small derived images of F and P. Use Localization.lift for the original localization Q at quasi-isomorphisms and Localization.fac to send that isomorphism back to the originally chosen universe w; compose with the given isomorphism from Q(F) to C. Translate the strict support bounds on P into the explicit IsZero bounds. No unit statement or unit proof step is bypassed: this reuses the existing proof of this very node.
